title: packetized-throughput-stitch-notebook-jordan
content:
Objective:
- Quick exploratory run to understand how request packetization (batching at the ingress layer in small 'packets' vs full request coalescing) affects throughput and tail latencies in the multi-tenant hosted runtime.
- Hypothesis: packetized ingress can reduce queuing jitter under mixed short/long sequences by letting smaller items flow sooner, improving p99 at modest QPS when cold/warm cache mix present, but might reduce peak throughput due to less efficient GPU utilization.

Environment / infra:
- Cluster: staging-serving-12 (4x A100s, 64 vCPU per node, 512GB RAM)
- Runtime build: serving-runtime:main @ commit 2b7f4c (PR 982 experimental ingress scheduler)
- Model: open-llama-7b-quant (int8) pinned to model-variant: q4_0_kvcache
- Instances: 8 replicas behind ingress balancer (round-robin)
- Observability: prometheus + grafana dashboard shard: packetized-experiments; traces sampled at 1%

Load generator / commands:
- Custom harness: bench-client v0.3 (nodejs) with arrival mixing. Key args used: 
  - --qps=300 --duration=600s --arrival=zipfian:1.2 --seq-len-dist="short:70%,medium:20%,long:10%" --packetize=true --packet-size=4
- For control: same config with --packetize=false
- Sample curl (single trace):
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/complete -d '{"input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":128}'

Experiment matrix (swept):
- Packetize: true | false
- Packet size: 2, 4, 8 (when packetize=true)
- QPS: 100, 300, 600
- Warm cache ratio: 30%, 70% (simulated by prewarm-phase)
- Repeats: 3 runs per cell (median reported)

Key metrics collected (per run): p50, p95, p99, p999 latencies (ms), end-to-end throughput (req/s achieved), GPU token/s, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate, 95th percentile queue length.

Representative results (median of 3 runs) [selected cells summarized]:

Case A: QPS=300, warm=70%
- packetize=false: p50=42ms, p95=180ms, p99=340ms, p999=720ms, throughput=298 req/s, avg batch size=12, gpu_token_s=2.1M, kv_hit=0.71, q95_queue=8
- packetize=true, size=4: p50=45ms, p95=160ms, p99=260ms, p999=520ms, throughput=284 req/s, avg batch size=9, gpu_token_s=1.95M, kv_hit=0.68, q95_queue=5

Case B: QPS=600, warm=70%
- packetize=false: p50=48ms, p95=260ms, p99=540ms, p999=1200ms, throughput=585 req/s, avg batch size=14, gpu_token_s=3.9M, kv_hit=0.69, q95_queue=18
- packetize=true, size=4: p50=55ms, p95=300ms, p99=680ms, p999=1450ms, throughput=560 req/s, avg batch size=10, gpu_token_s=3.1M, kv_hit=0.66, q95_queue=12

Case C: QPS=300, warm=30% (more cold activity)
- packetize=false: p50=58ms, p95=420ms, p99=880ms, p999=>2000ms (tail storms), throughput=290 req/s, avg batch size=11, gpu_token_s=2.0M, kv_hit=0.45, q95_queue=22
- packetize=true, size=4: p50=52ms, p95=220ms, p99=360ms, p999=820ms, throughput=275 req/s, avg batch size=8, gpu_token_s=1.75M, kv_hit=0.42, q95_queue=10

Observations / interpretation:
- Packetization reduces extreme tail (p99/p999) significantly when the workload includes a mix of short & long sequences and there is a meaningful cold cache ratio. Example: Case C p99 dropped from 880ms -> 360ms (size=4).
- The tradeoff is predictable: lower average batch size and lower GPU token/s; peak throughput drops ~3–7% in our tests, more noticeable at higher QPS (Case B).
- Packetization helps queue length spikes, keeping p95 and p99 down by allowing small requests to escape long coalescing waits. This is effectively reducing head-of-line blocking.
- Larger packet sizes (8) start to revert benefits: they look more like conventional batching and reintroduce p99 regressions under cold-heavy mixes. Packet-size=2 gives slightly better p50 but less p99 improvement vs size=4.

Telemetry notes:
- Traces show reduced number of long-tail kernel launches when packetize=true: fewer megabatches formed that mix long sequences with short ones.
- KV cache metrics: packetization reduces effective hit rate slightly (micro effect) because fewer requests were combined into the same batch slot, but the latency benefits for user-perceived tails outweighed the small hit-rate drop in our scenarios.

Quick recommendations for next steps:
- Run focused sweep around packet-size=3..5 at QPS 150-450 and warm ratios 10%,30%,50% to find Pareto frontier (latency vs throughput).
- Test on 8xA100 and on smaller GPU types (T4 / A10) to see if throughput drop is larger on memory/compute-constrained devices.
- Add realistic background noise: scheduled large-batch maintenance jobs to see stability under interference.
- Implement 'adaptive packetize' rule: packetize only when predicted average seq length < threshold or when tail latency starts to drift above SLO.

Quick TODOs (me / follow-ups):
- [ ] Push a small patch to bench-client to emit per-request batch-id (makes correlation with traces trivial) — assigned Mira.
- [ ] Add histogram export for per-packet batch build time to Prometheus — Jordan.
- [ ] Open a follow-up Linear ticket to try hybrid strategy (short-first fast-path + bulk coalesce) — done: INF-423 (linked above).

Notes / loose thoughts:
- Could be valuable to expose packetize as a per-route hint so customers can opt-in for latency-sensitive endpoints and accept the throughput delta.
- Customer UX: show estimated throughput/latency tradeoff in Console Optimize tab when toggling packetize setting.
- Potential ML idea: predict which requests should be 'fast-lane' (packetized) based on prompt length, tokenizing cost, and historical completion time.

Raw commands used (for reproducibility) — example run (Case C, packetize=true size=4):
bench-client --target=https://staging.api.redwood/complete --key=$TEST_KEY --qps=300 --duration=600 --arrival=zipfian:1.2 --seq-len-dist="short:70%,medium:20%,long:10%" --packetize=true --packet-size=4 --warm-ratio=30 --emit-batch-id > run_caseC_packet4.log 2>&1

Attached artifacts (local):
- run_caseC_packet4.log (prom + client output)
- grafana-snapshot-2026-02-20_packet4_caseC.png
- traces_sample_caseC_packet4.json

Overall: promising approach to reduce tails; clear tradeoffs. Next runs to tighten packet-size sweep and test cross-GPU behavior.

End of scratchpad.
